expectedText:
MINOR WORK PERMITS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme Corp

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's work-permit requirement for minors employed in California — the statutory process by which Jordan Alex Lee, a minor considered for or holding the position of Retail Associate with Acme Corp, and Jordan Alex Lee's parent or legal guardian, Taylor Morgan, obtain the work permit that Jordan Alex Lee's school, Lincoln High School, is authorized to issue, and the obligations that fall on Acme Corp once Jordan Alex Lee is employed. It states facts about what the Education Code's Permits to Work article and the related Labor Code provisions require. This corpus separately includes an I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification — Information Sheet, which addresses a different, federal requirement — verifying that a new hire of any age is authorized to work in the United States. The work-permit requirement described here is a distinct, California-specific, age-based requirement that applies in addition to, not instead of, federal I-9 verification. This document is not itself a work permit, a permit application, or a certificate of age, and it does not tell Acme Corp, Jordan Alex Lee, or Taylor Morgan what to do about any particular hire, application, or permit.

WHO COUNTS AS A "MINOR" UNDER THIS FRAMEWORK
For purposes of the Labor Code chapter governing the occupational privileges and restrictions of minors, "minor" is a defined term. It includes any person under the age of 18 who is required to attend school under the Education Code's compulsory-attendance provisions, and, separately, any person under the age of six, regardless of school-attendance status.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "“Minor” means any person under the age of 18 years who is required to attend school under Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 48200) and Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 48400) of Part 27 of Division 4 of Title 2 of the Education Code and any person under the age of six years."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1286(c) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, Chapter 2 (Occupational Privileges and Restrictions), definition of “minor” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1286.)
  Known gap: This document quotes only Labor Code § 1286(c)'s definition of "minor" for purposes of Labor Code Chapter 2 (Occupational Privileges and Restrictions). It did not independently fetch or verify the compulsory-attendance provisions that definition cross-references (Education Code §§ 48200 and 48400 et seq.), and it does not address the separate sentence in § 1286(c) covering a minor under 18 who is not required to attend California schools solely because of nonresident status.

WHO MAY ISSUE A WORK PERMIT, AND HOW THE PROCESS STARTS
California channels the work-permit process through the minor's school rather than through the employer. A work permit may be issued by the superintendent of the school district where the minor resides; the chief executive officer (or equivalent) of a charter school the minor attends; a school employee holding a pupil personnel services credential, or a certificated work-experience-education teacher or coordinator, authorized in writing by that superintendent or chief executive officer; the county superintendent of schools, for a minor outside any district's jurisdiction; or, subject to further statutory conditions, the principal of the public or private school the minor attends. The process does not begin with the employer: a work permit cannot be issued at all until a written request for it — from the minor's parent, guardian, foster parent, caregiver with whom the minor resides, or a residential-shelter-services provider — has been filed with whichever official is acting as the issuing authority.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "(b) Any of the following individuals may issue a work permit to a minor subject to the requirements and conditions of this chapter: (1) The superintendent of a school district in which the minor resides. (2) The chief executive officer, or the equivalent position, of a charter school that the minor attends. (3) A person holding a services credential with a specialization in pupil personnel services authorized by the superintendent of the school district or chief executive officer in writing, or a certificated work experience education teacher or coordinator authorized by the superintendent of the school district or chief executive officer in writing. (4) If the minor resides in a portion of a county not under the jurisdiction of the superintendent of a school district and does not attend a charter school, the county superintendent of schools, a person holding a services credential with a specialization in pupil personnel services authorized by the county superintendent of schools in writing, or a certificated work experience education teacher or coordinator authorized by the county superintendent of schools in writing may issue a work permit. (5) Subject to the requirements and conditions in subparagraphs (A) to (C), inclusive, the principal of a public or private school may issue, or designate another administrator in the school to issue, work permits to pupils who attend the school."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 49110(b) (California Legislative Information text), California Education Code, Permits to Work article, individuals authorized to issue a work permit (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=49110.)
  "(c) A work permit shall not be issued until the written request for the permit from the parent, guardian, foster parent, caregiver with whom the minor resides, or residential shelter services provider, has been filed with the issuing authority."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 49110(c) (California Legislative Information text), California Education Code, Permits to Work article, written-request prerequisite (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=49110.)
  Known gap: Both citations below are subdivisions of the same statute, Education Code § 49110 — subdivision (b) (who may issue a permit) and subdivision (c) (the written-request prerequisite) — not two independent sources. This document does not quote § 49110(a) (a legislative-intent statement about issuer training), (d), (e), or (f) (backup-issuer authority and how school-calendar-based hour limits apply to a permit), nor subparagraphs (A) through (C) under paragraph (b)(5), which impose self-certification, superintendent-revocation, and no-issuing-to-one's-own-child conditions specifically on a principal who issues permits.

THE PERMIT TO EMPLOY, EMPLOYER RECORDKEEPING, AND EXPIRATION
The permit system has an employer-facing side as well. The same official authorized to issue permits to work or to employ may issue a certificate of age to a minor who appears with a parent, guardian, or other person in control of the minor and presents the required evidence of age; that certificate of age itself serves as the permit to employ a minor who is not legally required to attend school but who is otherwise required to hold a permit to work. Once a minor is employed, the employer — directly or through anyone acting on the employer's behalf — must keep on file all such permits and certificates, whether to work or to employ, issued under the Labor Code chapter or under the Education Code's minors-employment provisions, and must keep those files open at all times to inspection by school attendance and probation officers, the State Board of Education, and the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement. A permit to work issued during the school year does not last indefinitely: it expires five days after the opening of the next school year.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "The person authorized to issue permits to work or to employ may issue to any minor a certificate of age when the minor accompanied by his parent, guardian, or other person in control or charge of the minor, presents to the authority, the evidence of age specified in this chapter. The certificate of age shall serve as a permit to employ a minor who is not by law required to attend school, and who is otherwise required to hold a permit to work."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 49114 (California Legislative Information text), California Education Code, certificate of age serving as a permit to employ (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=49114.)
  "Every person, or agent or officer thereof, employing minors, either directly or indirectly through third persons, shall keep on file all permits and certificates, either to work or to employ, issued under this chapter or Part 27 (commencing with Section 48000) of the Education Code. The files shall be open at all times to the inspection of the school attendance and probation officers, the State Board of Education, and the officers of the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1299 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, employer recordkeeping and inspection of minor-employment permits (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1299.)
  "Permits to work issued during the school year shall expire five days after the opening of the next succeeding school year."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 49118 (California Legislative Information text), California Education Code, expiration of a school-year work permit (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=49118.)
  Known gap: This clause combines three separate statutes — Education Code § 49114 (certificate of age / permit to employ), Labor Code § 1299 (employer recordkeeping), and Education Code § 49118 (expiration) — because together they describe the employer-facing half of the same permit system; none of the three is a subdivision of either of the other two. This document did not verify what specific "evidence of age" § 49114 requires beyond its own general cross-reference, and it did not verify whether or how a permit to work issued outside the school year (for example, under Education Code § 49111, for vacation-period employment) expires, since § 49118 by its own terms addresses only permits "issued during the school year."

HOUR AND TIME-OF-DAY LIMITS, AND REVOCATION FOR IMPAIRMENT
Separate from the permit-issuance process, the Labor Code directly limits when and how long a minor may work, keyed to age and to whether school is in session. A minor 15 or younger may not be employed more than eight hours in a day or 40 hours in a week, or before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. (extended to 9 p.m. from June 1 through Labor Day); while school is in session, that drops to no more than three hours on a schoolday or 18 hours in a week, never during school hours, with an exception for a minor enrolled in a school-supervised work-experience and career-exploration program (up to 23 hours). A minor 16 or 17 may not be employed more than eight hours in a day or 48 hours in a week, or before 5 a.m. or after 10 p.m. on a night before a schoolday (extended to 12:30 a.m. before a nonschoolday); while school is in session, that drops to no more than four hours on a schoolday, subject to listed exceptions including personal-attendant occupations, school-approved work experience, cooperative vocational education, and a minor who has been issued a permit to work under Education Code § 49112(c). "Schoolday" for these limits means any day the minor is required to attend school for 240 minutes or more. Separately, the authority that issued a minor's permit to work may revoke it if shown, to that authority's satisfaction, that the minor's schoolwork or health is being impaired by the employment.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "(a) Except as provided in Sections 1297, 1298, and 1308.7: (1) An employer shall not employ a minor 15 years of age or younger for more than eight hours in one day of 24 hours, or more than 40 hours in one week, or before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m., except that from June 1 through Labor Day, a minor 15 years of age or younger may be employed for the hours authorized by this section until 9 p.m. in the evening. (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), while school is in session, an employer shall not employ a minor 14 or 15 years of age for more than three hours in any schoolday, nor more than 18 hours in any week, nor during school hours, except that a minor enrolled in and employed pursuant to a school-supervised and school-administered work experience and career exploration program may be employed for no more than 23 hours, any portion of which may be during school hours. (3) An employer shall not employ a minor 16 or 17 years of age for more than eight hours in one day of 24 hours or more than 48 hours in one week, or before 5 a.m., or after 10 p.m. on any day preceding a schoolday. However, a minor 16 or 17 years of age may be employed for the hours authorized by this section during any evening preceding a nonschoolday until 12:30 a.m. of the nonschoolday. (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3), while school is in session, an employer shall not employ a minor 16 or 17 years of age for more than four hours in any schoolday, except as follows: (A) The minor is employed in personal attendant occupations, as defined in the Industrial Welfare Commission Minimum Wage Order No. 15 (8 Cal. Code Regs. Sec. 11150), school-approved work experience, or cooperative vocational education programs. (B) The minor has been issued a permit to work pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 49112 of the Education Code and is employed in accordance with the provisions of that permit. (b) For purposes of this section, “schoolday” means any day in which a minor is required to attend school for 240 minutes or more."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 1391(a)-(b) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, age-based hour and time-of-day limits on employing a minor (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1391.)
  "(c) If evidence is shown, to the satisfaction of the authority issuing the permit to work, that the schoolwork or the health of the minor is being impaired by the employment, that authority may revoke the permit."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 49116(c) (California Legislative Information text), California Education Code, revocation of a work permit for impairment of schoolwork or health (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=49116.)
  Known gap: The hour limits quoted here come from Labor Code § 1391. Education Code § 49116(a)-(b) states hour limits for 14-15 and 16-17 year-olds that closely track Labor Code § 1391(a)(2) and (a)(4); to avoid presenting the same restriction as if it came from two independent sources, this document cites only Labor Code § 1391 for the hour limits themselves and cites Education Code § 49116 only for its distinct subdivision (c), the impairment-based revocation rule that § 1391 does not itself contain. This document does not address the separate, generally different hour and time limits that apply to minors in the entertainment industry under Labor Code § 1308.7, which § 1391(a) expressly carves out of its own coverage, or the misdemeanor penalties § 1391(c) attaches to a violation.

EXEMPTION FOR MINORS WHO HAVE ALREADY GRADUATED HIGH SCHOOL (OR ITS EQUIVALENT)
The entire Education Code chapter governing the employment of minors — and, by extension, the work-permit mechanics described above — does not apply to a minor who has already graduated from a four-year high school course above the eighth grade, who has had an equivalent amount of education in a private school or by private tuition, or who has been awarded a certificate of proficiency under Education Code § 48412.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-03]
  "The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any minor who has been graduated from a high school maintaining a four-year course above the eighth grade of elementary schools, or who has had an equal amount of education in a private school or by private tuition, or who has been awarded a certificate of proficiency pursuant to Section 48412 of the Education Code."
  — Cal. Educ. Code § 49101 (California Legislative Information text), California Education Code, exemption for a minor who has graduated high school or its equivalent (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=EDC&sectionNum=49101.)
  Known gap: This document examined the Education Code sections in Part 27, Chapter 7 (the work-permit chapter) but did not find, and so does not assert, a separate express statutory exemption specifically naming emancipated minors within the sections it reviewed; it also did not independently fetch or verify Education Code § 48412 (the certificate-of-proficiency provision this exemption cross-references), or Education Code § 49102 through § 49104, section numbers that returned no content when queried directly and that this document therefore treats as not currently in force rather than as a source of any additional exemption. A reader whose situation may involve emancipation, home schooling, or a certificate of proficiency should not assume any of those is or is not covered based on this document alone.

SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATION
Please sign below to indicate receipt and review of this information sheet.

Minor: Jordan Alex Lee
Position: Retail Associate
Employer: Acme Corp
School: Lincoln High School
Date: _______________

Parent or legal guardian: Taylor Morgan
Date: _______________

Acme Corp certifies that this information sheet was provided to Jordan Alex Lee and Taylor Morgan in connection with the position of Retail Associate, with an anticipated start date of September 15, 2026.

Company representative: _______________
